chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Muhammad ibn Khalid and Al-Husayn ibn Sa'id, altogether from Al-Qasim ibn 'Urwa, from Hisham ibn Salim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

The Tasbih of Fatima Al-Zahra (peace be upon her): When you take to your bed, glorify Allah (say Allahu Akbar) thirty-four times, praise Him (say Al-Hamd Lillah) thirty-three times, and glorify Him (say Subhan Allah) thirty-three times, and recite Ayat Al-Kursi, and the two Mu'awwidhatayn (Surahs Al-Falaq and An-Nas), and ten verses from the beginning of Surah Al-Saffat, and ten verses from its end.

key_terms.آيَةَ الْكُرْسِيِّ: Ayat Al-Kursi (The Verse of the Throne, Quran 2:255)
key_terms.الْمُعَوِّذَتَيْنِ: The two Surahs of protection (Al-Falaq and An-Nas)
key_terms.تَسْبِيحُ فَاطِمَةَ الزَّهْرَاءِ: Tasbih of Fatima Al-Zahra, a specific devotional prayer

ai.seo_question: What is the Tasbih of Fatima Al-Zahra and how is it performed before sleep?
ai.summary: Recorded in Al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) codifies the nightly dhikr of Fatima al-Zahra (SA), linking the specific numerical structure of glorification to the recitation of Ayat al-Kursi, Al-Mu'awwidhatayn, and a unique selection from Surah As-Saffat. This practice underscores the Shia emphasis on the domestic spiritual discipline of the Ahl al-Bayt, serving as a protective shield against spiritual and physical disturbances during sleep. The inclusion of Surah As-Saffat highlights the thematic connection between divine protection and the remembrance of God's sovereignty over creation.
